event: CARES Act forbearance begins. Federal agencies issue written guidance to FHA, VA and USDA servicers stating paused payments are repaid over time and a lump sum is not required.

event: The COVID-19 Veterans Assistance Partial Claim Payment program expires by regulation. VA will not accept a request for a partial claim payment after October 28, 2022. No replacement tool exists for VA borrowers exiting forbearance.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-07-26. The expiry is in the regulation itself, subsection (c), the absolute cutoff. Earlier draft cited 36.4803, which is the eligibility section, not the expiration section.

event: The years with no partial claim. Families exit forbearance on terms the 2020 guidance ruled out.

event: VBA Circular 26-23-25. VA strongly encourages a foreclosure moratorium on all VA-guaranteed loans through May 31, 2024, urging servicers to cease initiating, continuing or completing foreclosures. Stated reason includes the pending availability of VASP, which the circular places in March 2024.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-07-27. Stage one of the moratorium chain. Note the March 2024 VASP date, which slipped to May 31, 2024. Broader than the 2024 version: all VA-guaranteed loans, excluding vacant or abandoned.

event: House Veterans' Affairs Committee hearing. The partial claim gap and foreclosure exposure are raised directly, three months before VASP launches.
notes: Receipt: hearing-2024-authority.png, hearing-2024-rate.png

event: VA announces VASP, stating the program will help more than 40,000 veterans stay in their homes, and says it has strongly encouraged a foreclosure moratorium through May 31, 2024.
notes: The 40,000 figure is VA's own. Useful against any claim that the affected population was unknown or small.

event: VBA Circular 26-24-12, Loan Repayment Relief for Borrowers. VA announces a targeted foreclosure moratorium on VA-guaranteed loans running through December 31, 2024, stating its purpose is to give servicers time to implement VASP. Servicers may implement beginning May 31, 2024. VA expects full implementation not later than October 1, 2024. Circular valid until January 1, 2025.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-07-27 from the circular PDF. This is the precedent row. VA itself documents that launch date does not equal availability, and that a launch-to-readiness gap warrants a foreclosure moratorium. Paragraph 1 = purpose and dates. Paragraph 3 = moratorium scope, four exceptions. Paragraph 10 = validity. Compare directly to T023.

event: VA press release announcing the extension. Describes the moratorium as originally slated to expire May 31 and states that VASP officially launches May 31 and mortgage servicers must have it fully implemented by October 1, 2024. Under Secretary for Benefits Josh Jacobs is quoted calling on servicers to follow the targeted moratorium.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-07-27. Stage two. The release says must have it fully implemented, firmer than the circular's expects. Pairs with T025.

event: VASP is implemented as the final option in the VA Home Retention Waterfall.

event: VA's own full-implementation deadline for VASP. From this date to the May 1, 2025 rescission is roughly seven months of broadly usable program, not the twelve months the period is commonly described as.
notes: Counter to the May 2024 to May 2025 full-year framing. Calendar measurement vs availability measurement.

The CFO answers that the account structure co-mingles costs: "all I can tell you is that it's going to cost more and that we can't manage to it because we don't know where we're managing to." The testimony concerns VA's health care account structure, not the home loan program.

notes: Hearing category: VA OVERSIGHT. The 2026-05-20 SVAC hearing covered VA benefits, programs and funding broadly, including home loans, foreclosures and VASP. It is where Sen. Blumenthal put the 15,000+ figure on the record and where the June 15 commitment was made. Do not describe it as a healthcare hearing. On this specific quotation: the exchange with Chairman Moran concerned how VA reports spending and the CFO said the account structure co-mingles costs, concluding 'We do not know what we are managing.'
